rules.name: T15 three-middle closed form (now proved for all r>=4, all nm)
rules.description_text: Domain: r>=4, r divides no a_i, exactly three a_i have residue a_i mod r in [2,r-2], and every other a_i has residue 1 or r-1. (If some a_i is divisible by r, predict True.) Compute D = sum(a_i-1). Compute the class sums Gamma_t (t mod r) of prod over the parts with residue >=2 of [a_i mod r]_q, reduced mod q^r-1, and set tau_t = Gamma_t - Gamma_{t-1}. (This equals the residue-class sums of (1-q)prod[a_i]_q.) Set mu = the largest j in [1,r-1] with tau_j>0, or 0 if there is none. Set T6 = 1+floor((D+1-2mu)/r), s = (D+1) mod r, FIRE = (tau_s <= -2 and s >= 2mu), and B* = T6 - 2*FIRE. Predict that P is unimodal iff b <= B*.

rules.name: rule_gen (four middle residues: residue-level closed form with the nontrivial-part count k')
rules.description_text: Domain: r>=4, r divides no a_i, exactly four a_i have a residue in [2,r-2], and every other a_i has residue 1 or r-1. Step 1: drop the parts equal to 1. Let k' be the number of remaining parts, D = sum(a_i-1), tau = (1-q)*prod_i [a_i mod r]_q reduced mod q^r-1 (tau_t for t in Z/r), mu = max{j in [1,r-1]: tau_j>0} (0 if there is none), and T6 = 1+floor((D+1-2mu)/r). Let f_i be the coefficients of 1/((1-q)^(k'-1)(1-q^r)), i.e. f_i = sum_{m>=0} C(i-rm+k'-2, k'-2), with f_i = 0 for i<0. predict(b) is true if b <= T6-2. It is false if b > T6. For b in {T6-1, T6}, put K = D+1-r(b+1) and m0 = max(1, -floor((K-1)/2)). Then b is predicted unimodal iff (a) f_{K+m} + tau_{(-m) mod r} >= 0 for every m in [m0, min(r*b, m0+r)], and (b) either K < 1 or 1 - f_K <= tau_0. Consequently U = [1,T6-2] ∪ {T6-1 if LOW(T6-1)} ∪ {T6 if LOW(T6)}. The rule depends only on (r, tau, D, k'), and the correction affects at most the two values T6-1 and T6. Background: this is a truncation of the K-form of Thm A, which I derived (P_b unimodal iff g_j - g_{K-j} <= tau_j for -rb <= j <= floor((K-1)/2), with g = A/[r]_q). Here the actual g is replaced by its 'generic' value f. Conjecture, not proved: (1) [1,T6-2] ⊆ U; (2) the conditions outside the window hold automatically; (3) the actual g and the generic f give the same verdict.

Random checks: about 9,300 instances with r<=120 and 2,400 tiny-part instances, plus hill-climbing. Weak spot check: 40 instances with r in [1000,1400], none of which activates the correction.

proofs.statement: Theorem N: For exactly four middle residues (other residues 1 or r-1), no function of (r, k, b, residue multiset, F, D, Gamma vector), even with sum(a_i) and prod(a_i) added, decides unimodality. The proof uses Lemma 2: Gamma = Gamma(prod[s_i]_q) + ((prod a - prod s)/r)*(1,...,1), so equal sum, product and residue multiset force identical Gamma, tau, mu, T6, F and D. The witness r=20, a=(1,14,59,65,79,105,123) gives U=[1,20], while a'=(3,14,21,59,65,79,205) gives U=[1,22]; two further witnesses are included. The cause is that g_1 = #{a_i>=2} - 1 enters the j=-1 condition at b=T6-1 with K=0.

failure_report: The path partly succeeded, and the main caveat is this. A closed form at the Gamma level (r, Gamma/tau, D, F) does not exist, and this is proved by exact witness pairs. But every witness relies on parts a_i = 1: they leave P unchanged but change k' = #{a_i >= 2}, which Gamma, D and F do not see. With k' added, rule_gen.py (which uses only r, tau, D, k') fits every tested instance with 0 errors. Its form is U = [1,T6-2] plus up to two more values, T6-1 and T6, each decided by about r inequalities f_{K+m} + tau_{-m} >= 0 (f = coefficients of 1/((1-q)^(k'-1)(1-q^r))) and one j=0 test. I did not prove it: the claims [1,T6-2] ⊆ U, that the window suffices, and that the actual g and the generic f agree are all conjectural. Instances with r >= 1000 were tested only weakly (40 instances, none with the correction active). The T15 formula alone has 18 errors on the main sample, so the four-middle case really does need the low-order (k') correction.

rules.name: R3E7-STAB (hybrid zero-pattern rule; gives sharp L0 = L0_hyb)
rules.description_text: Setup: r divides no a_i, all a_i>=2. Let s be the residues a_i mod r, k=len(a), S=sum s, K0=S-k+1, F=sum floor(a_i/r). tau = residue-class sums of (1-q)prod[s_i]_q reduced mod q^r-1. w_n=[q^n]1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)) (0 for n<0). Delta_e=K0-r(e+1), W(Delta)={m: Delta/2<m<=Delta/2+r}. U_inf={1} u {e in [2,T]: w_m - w_{Delta_e-m} >= tau_{m mod r} for all m in W(Delta_e)}, T=1+floor((K0-2mu)/r), mu=max{t in [0,r-1]: tau_t>0}. Hybrid test for a multiset Z of small parts: h^Z = prod_{z in Z}(1-q^z) * w (coefficientwise; equivalently prod[z]_q/((1-q)^{k-1-|Z|}(1-q^r))); H(Z) holds iff h^Z_m - h^Z_{Delta_e-m} >= tau_{m mod r} for every e in U_inf with e>=2 and every m in W(Delta_e). DOMAIN: r divides no a_i, min a_i>=2, and H(Z(a)) where Z(a) = the parts a_i < r. PREDICT: P unimodal iff b<=F+1 or b-F in U_inf. Sharp threshold formula: L0*(r,s) = least t>=2 with H({s_i : s_i>=t}). This is proved to be a lower bound for L0*, conjectured equal, and it is always <= max(s)+1 <= r. Proved part: on the subdomain min a_i >= max(2, floor(Delta_{e2}/2)+r+1), e2=min(U_inf\{1}), the prediction is a theorem. Monotone part: if the prediction holds for a, it also holds for every lift of a by multiples of r.

proofs.statement: (Lemma 2/Cor 3) Stability, meaning U(a)=[1,F]u(F+U_inf(r,s)), is preserved by lifting any part by r. So the stable instances form an up-set in the quotient vector. (Prop 4) The sharp L0*(r,s) = least L>=2 such that a^L is stable, where a^L_i is the least value >=L congruent to s_i. The set of such L is an up-ray, and L0* <= max(2, floor(Delta_{e2}/2)+r+1) <= max(2, floor((S-k+3-r)/2)).

(Prop 6, Cor 7) Let H(Z) be the hybrid test with h^Z = prod_{z in Z}(1-q^z)/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)). H(Z) holds iff the instance with Z at residue values and all other parts very large is stable. H is monotone, stable(a) implies H(Z(a)), and L0_hyb = min{t>=2: H({s_i>=t})} satisfies L0_hyb <= L0* and L0_hyb <= max(s)+1 <= r.

(Thm 8) The sharp L0* is not a function of (r,k,S,tau), which is the data fixing U_inf. With r=7, s=(1,1,3,4,4,4,4,5,5) gives L0*=2 and s'=(1,2,2,4,4,4,4,4,6) gives L0*=3. (Thm 9) Stabilization is not determined by (residue multiset, a_min). With r=5, (2,7,8^7) is stable and (2,2,8^7) is not, both with a_min=2. The proofs use Prop 4 plus a finite exact computation with uni.

failure_report: The path worked partly. I did not find a closed form for the sharp L0 in terms of r, k and residue statistics; the formula found is a finite residue-level test. Any formula depending only on (r,k,S,tau) is impossible (Thm 8, proved). Six closed-form or approximate candidates were rejected, with error counts in candidates.txt. The exact formula L0* = L0_hyb is proved only as a lower bound, L0_hyb <= L0*. Equality, and the bound L0* <= max(s)+1 <= r, are Conjecture Q / Q1. These have 0 counterexamples in the fit box but no proof. The hard step is showing that a part of quotient exactly 1 is as harmless as an infinite part. The deficit is a sum of Ahat_{m-c} - Ahat_{y-c} terms against the hybrid slack, and I found no structural inequality bounding it.

rules.name: B: zero-parameter rotation-word closed form for U in the large-part regime (exact log-binomial)
rules.description_text: Domain: r divides no a_i, k>=3, at least one residue s_i=a_i mod r in [2,r-2], and min a_i >= max(1, floor((S-k+3-r)/2)), where S = sum s_i. Prediction: let F = sum floor(a_i/r), S1 = sum(s_i-1), K0 = S1+1. If b <= F+1, predict unimodal. Otherwise put e = b-F. Let l = sum_i ln( sin(pi s_i/r)/sin(pi/r) ). Let theta solve (1+t)ln(1+t) - t ln t = l/k, lambda = ln(1+1/theta), rho = e^lambda. For each chain parity eps in {1 (odd e), 0 (even e)}: the lattice is u in {1,...,r} if K0 - r(eps+1) is even, and u in {1/2, 3/2, ..., r-1/2} otherwise. Put g(u) = (4 sin(pi/r)/r) * (-1)^eps * sin(2 pi u/r), and keep only the u with g(u) > 0. For each kept u, let n_u be the least real n with lnGamma(n+u+k-1) - lnGamma(k-1) - lnGamma(n+u+1) + ln((1-rho^(-2u))/(1-rho^(-r))) >= l + ln g(u), found by bisection. Let nu_eps = max_u n_u and X_eps = (K0 - r - 2 nu_eps)/r. Then e_odd = max(1, largest odd integer <= X_1) and e_even = max(0, largest even integer <= X_0). Predict unimodal iff (e odd and e <= e_odd) or (e even and e <= e_even). Variant A (rule_asym.py) is the fully explicit form. It replaces the log-binomial by its Stirling linearisation, which gives nu_eps = theta k + ln k/(2 lambda) + (psi_eps - c0)/lambda, where psi_eps = max over kept u of [ln g(u) - lambda u - ln((1-rho^(-2u))/(1-rho^(-r)))] and c0 = -1.5 ln(1+theta) - 0.5 ln theta - 0.5 ln(2 pi). So X_1 = c k - kappa ln k + gamma(parity of S1+1), with c = (S1/k - 2 theta)/r and kappa = 1/(r lambda). In words, the O(1) term of E = e_odd - 1 is a two-state function (the parity of S1+1) of the fractional part of an explicit real sequence: a rotation word with a logarithmic drift.
rules.fit_range: Two parts. (1) Fit box r<=120, k<=140 at residue level (excluded classes skipped): 173 random families (block repeated, k = m*len(block)), 7245 (family,k) points, plus sweep2 runs (6047 points). The instance level used a_i<=400, r in [4,120], k in [3,40] and exact ground truth gt_big.py: 124047 (r,a,b) checks. (2) r>=1000 families: r=1000 block(500,1) k<=998; r=1001 block(300,650,1) k<=498; r=1009 block(400,700,1) k<=1059; r=1200 block(77) k<=556; r=2000 block(999,1999,1) k<=345. This is 1686 points.

rules.name: A: fully explicit linearised closed form (same structure, Stirling-linearised)
rules.description_text: Same domain and same chain-top rule as rule B. The difference is nu_eps = theta k + ln k/(2 lambda) + (psi_eps - c0)/lambda, where psi_eps = max over lattice u with g(u)>0 of [ln g(u) - lambda u - ln((1-rho^(-2u))/(1-rho^(-r)))], with g(u) = (4 sin(pi/r)/r)(-1)^eps sin(2 pi u/r) and c0 = -1.5 ln(1+theta) - 0.5 ln theta - 0.5 ln(2 pi). Then X_eps = (S1 + 1 - r - 2 nu_eps)/r, e_odd = max(1, largest odd <= X_1) and e_even = max(0, largest even <= X_0). Predict unimodal iff b <= F+1, or e = b-F is odd with e <= e_odd, or e is even with 2 <= e <= e_even. Along a family this gives E(k) = 2 floor((c k - kappa ln k + gamma_1 - 1)/2), with gamma_1 = (1-r)/r - 2(ln(4 sin(pi/r)/r) + psi_1' - c0)/(lambda r) depending only on the parity of S1+1. Here psi_1' is psi_1 without the amplitude constant.

Fitted alternatives are worse than the zero-parameter rule B (52 errors): one beta per family gives 73/7245 errors, and one beta per family and S1 parity gives 55/7245. Eventually periodic increments with period <=12 fail for 73 of 126 families

The model gap delta = X_odd - X_even lies in (1.00005, 1.086). So asymptotically e_even = e_odd - 1, except on a window of the rotation circle of width delta-1, where e_even = e_odd - 3 (the S2 shape)
The dominant-mode formula for tau on the window lattice has max abs error 1.3e-5 (relative to e^{l_1}), and the dominant set is always {1,r-1}

proofs.statement: Lemma 1: if some residue is middle, then l_1 = l_{r-1} > l_j for every other j. Lemma 2 (exact phase alignment): for m = Delta_e/2 + u, tau_m = (4 sin(pi/r)/r) e^{l_1} (-1)^e sin(2 pi u/r) + O(e^{l'}). So the dominant window profile depends on k only through the parity of S1+1.

Theorem 4 / Corollary 5: fix r>=4 and a block containing a middle residue, with k = m p. For every eps0>0 and m large, if X_1(k) is at least eps0 from the odd integers, then E(k) = 2 floor((X_1(k)-1)/2). Here X_1 = ck - kappa ln k + gamma_1(parity of S1+1) with explicit constants. The analogous statement holds for e_even with X_0. So the O(1) term is a two-state rotation word with logarithmic drift.

Proposition 6: along any family, E(k) - (ck - kappa ln k) is not eventually periodic in m, and the increments E((m+1)p) - E(mp) are not eventually periodic. The second part uses R2E6 Thm 3. Remark 7: in the model, delta = X_1 - X_0 > 1.

failure_report: The path did not fail, but four points limit the result. (1) Theorem 4 holds only outside eps0-windows around the thresholds. I did not prove whether the exceptional set is finite. With O(1/k) corrections the expected number of exceptions up to K grows like log K: infinitely many, but of density zero. (2) Pre-asymptotic errors are large when the spectral gap l_1 - l_2 per part is small, i.e. residues near 1 or r-1. Example: r=119, block (112), k in [14,52], where X is off by up to 0.39. Theorem 4 still holds there, but its m0 is large. (3) delta < 2 (asymptotic S2) is only numerical. (4) The irrationality of c is not needed and was not proved.
